## Rule

**Color permutation (ARC `0d3d703e`)** — every cell of color `c` → color `colormap[c]`,
with `colormap = (0,5,6,4,3,1,2,7,9,8)` = the involution `(1 5)(2 6)(3 4)(8 9)`, fixing
`{0,7}`. Geometry unchanged. The one-hot encoder puts color `c` on channel `c`, so the
rule is a pure **channel permutation on axis 1**.

Confirmed **2000/2000 fresh ARC-GEN** (UUID `0d3d703e`) vs the canonical Gather —
**genuine target, not a phantom** (task016 is NOT in the zero-public-weight family).
ARC-GEN inputs only ever contain 8 colors (`random_colors` excludes orange=7; bg=0 is
never a fill color), but `colormap` fixes both 0 and 7, so the canonical is correct on
all 10 channels — no unseen-color risk.

## Algorithm sketch

```
# one-hot input [1,10,30,30], channel == color; involution so inverse == colormap
output = Gather(input, idx=[0,5,6,4,3,1,2,7,9,8] (INT64 [10]), axis=1)   # output[j] = input[idx[j]]
```
Single node. `idx[10]` = 10 params; the Gather output IS the graph output (free) ⇒
memory 0 ⇒ **cost 10, points 22.6974**.

## Cost analysis

cost 10 = **params 10** (the `idx[10]` initializer) + **memory 0** (single node: the
Gather output is the graph output, which `calculate_memory` skips; there is no
intermediate `value_info`). `params` counts *elements*, so INT32/INT16/INT8 indices don't
help (and sub-INT32 Gather indices are rejected by the scorer — traps §8c). The output
`[1,10,30,30]` and the input are both free; no MAC term. ⇒ 10 is irreducible for a dense
single-Gather; the floor proof below shows nothing correct beats it.

## 🔒 10 = PROVEN single-Gather floor (2026-05-30 — PROVEN, DO NOT RE-ATTEMPT)

`cost = memory + params`; to beat 22.6974 a candidate must score **cost ≤ 9, byte-equal**.
Every angle in the prompt — **plus the sparse-storage angle the captain's note did not
cover** — was **built and scored via `score_network_v2`** and verified byte-equal vs the
canonical on random one-hots. Full measured table:

| candidate | cost | mem | par | correct? | why it can't win |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| **canonical Gather idx[10] INT64** | **10** | 0 | 10 | ✓ 2000/2000 | the floor |
| Gather idx[10] INT32 | 10 | 0 | 10 | ✓ | params = element count (dtype-agnostic) |
| Gather idx, **sparse_initializer** (9 nnz) | **None** | — | 9 | ✓ output | strict `shape_inference` rejects sparse Gather index → scorer `None` (unshippable) |
| Gather idx, **Constant(sparse_value)** INT64 | 89 | 80 | 9 | ✓ | params 9 ✔ but materialized `[10]` INT64 intermediate = 80 mem |
| Gather idx, **Constant(sparse_value)** INT32 | 49 | 40 | 9 | ✓ | params 9 ✔ but `[10]` INT32 intermediate = 40 mem (INT16/INT8 idx → `None`) |
| **Transpose-only** (perm attr, 0 params) | **0** | 0 | 0 | **✗ 0/64 WRONG** | Transpose permutes whole axes; **cannot** permute *within* the channel axis |
| Reshape[1,2,5,30,30]+Transpose+Reshape | 72009 | 72000 | 9 | ✗ 0/64 | perm is not a clean 2×5 block swap; + INT64 reshape intermediates |
| Split(10)→Concat (reorder) | 36010 | 36000 | 10 | ✓ | 10 channel-slice `[1,1,30,30]` intermediates = 36000 mem |
| per-channel Slice→Concat (partial-edit) | 36030 | 36000 | 30 | ✓ | every slice is a counted intermediate |
| Conv 1×1 permutation kernel | 100 | 0 | 100 | ✓ | weight `[10,10,1,1]` = 100 params |
| Conv 1×1 **sparse weight** (10 nnz) | **None** | — | 10 | ✓ output | scorer rejects sparse Conv weight (core.md) |
| MatMul permutation matrix | 72100 | 72000 | 100 | ✓ | transposes create `[1,30,30,10]` intermediates |
| dynamic Range+Add index | 173 | 160 | 13 | ✓ | Range/Add make `[10]` intermediates (160 mem) |
| GatherElements (full-rank index) | 9000 | 0 | 9000 | ✓ | index must be `[1,10,30,30]` = 9000 params |
| ScatterElements (base + full-rank idx) | 18000 | 0 | 18000 | ✓ | base 9000 + index 9000 params |

**The two-case proof** (why no correct, scoreable graph beats 10):

1. **memory = 0 ⟺ single node** (any 2nd node adds a counted `value_info` intermediate).
   The only correct single-node channel-permutation ops and their *irreducible* param
   counts: `Gather(idx[10])` = **10**; `Conv`/`MatMul` permutation matrix = **100**;
   `GatherElements`/`Scatter` full-rank index = **9000+**. The sole **zero-param** reorder
   op is `Transpose` (perm is a free attribute) — but it permutes *whole axes only* and
   **cannot** express a within-channel permutation (measured: cost 0, **0/64 WRONG**).
   The other "free reorder" ops are structurally inapplicable: `DepthToSpace`/`SpaceToDepth`
   rearrange channel↔spatial and **cannot keep shape `[1,10,30,30]`** (DepthToSpace needs
   `b²∣10` ⇒ only `b=1` identity; SpaceToDepth gives `10·b²≠10` channels for `b>1`) — no
   shape-valid graph exists. ⇒ min correct single-node cost = **10**.

2. **params < 10 ⟺ sparse index storage.** The index `[0,5,6,4,3,1,2,7,9,8]` has exactly
   **one** structural zero (position 0 = fixed channel 0), so sparse storage drops to 9
   stored values. But that "−1 param" is never free: a `sparse_initializer` consumed by
   Gather → scorer returns **`None`** (strict-mode rejection); a `Constant(sparse_value)`
   → params 9 ✔ but it **materializes a `[10]` dense intermediate** costing ≥40 B (INT32;
   sub-INT32 Gather indices are rejected, traps §8c) ⇒ cost ≥ **49**. ⇒ every params-9
   graph costs ≥ 49 > 10.

⇒ **No correct, scoreable graph scores below cost 10. The canonical single Gather is the
proven floor (points 22.6974).** This confirms the captain's hypothesis and additionally
closes the sparse gap the hypothesis did not address.

## Don't-do log

- **sub-10 is IMPOSSIBLE — PROVEN 2026-05-30 (see 🔒 floor section).** Do not spend
  worker-hours hunting cost<10 for task016. 15 candidates measured; every correct,
  scoreable one is ≥ 10. Three traps for anyone tempted: (a) **sparse index gets params 9
  but is either `None` (`sparse_initializer`) or +40/80 mem (`Constant(sparse_value)`)** —
  net ≥ 49; (b) **`Transpose` is free but can't permute within an axis** (0/64 wrong);
  (c) every Split/Slice/Reshape/MatMul data-path materializes ≥ 36000 B of channel
  intermediates. This is the task016 analogue of the task155=158 floor proof.
- **crop_to_active_grid advisory (2026-05-19)**: Advisory claims −35640 bytes savings, but the model is a **single Gather node** (cost=10, memory=0, params=10). The "1 [...,30,30] intermediate" the scanner sees is the model input or output, not a reducible intermediate. Adding Slice+Pad would only ADD overhead with no savings — the model already has essentially zero memory cost.
- **Recolor-family note (2026-05-30, [[task337]] probe):** the one clean sub-10 recolor op is a full-axis `Slice(starts=[9],ends=[-11],axes=[1],steps=[-1])` = channel reversal, **cost 4** (verified) — it beats the Gather floor ONLY for the exact reversal idx `[9,8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1,0]`. task016's idx `[0,5,6,4,3,1,2,7,9,8]` is a generic 8-channel perm, not a reversal ⇒ floor stays 10. (The proof table above lists Slice under multi-node reassembly; the full-axis reverse is the single-node exception, N/A here.)
